== Sounio ==

{{works with|Sounio|v1.0.0-beta.6}}

Sounio supports higher-order functions via named function references. Closure literals (<code>|x| x + 1</code>) are not supported — use named functions instead.

<lang sounio>fn double(x: i64) -> i64 { x * 2 }
fn is_even(x: i64) -> i64 { if x % 2 == 0 { 1 } else { 0 } }
fn square(x: i64) -> i64 { x * x }

fn map4(arr: [i64; 4], f: fn(i64) -> i64) -> [i64; 4] with Mut, Panic {
    var out: [i64; 4] = [0; 4]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 4 {
        out[i] = f(arr[i])
        i = i + 1
    }
    out
}

fn filter4(arr: [i64; 4], pred: fn(i64) -> i64) -> [i64; 4] with Mut, Panic {
    var out: [i64; 4] = [0; 4]
    var i: i64 = 0
    var j: i64 = 0
    while i < 4 {
        if pred(arr[i]) == 1 {
            out[j] = arr[i]
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }
    out
}

fn main() with IO, Mut, Panic, Div {
    let nums: [i64; 4] = [1, 2, 3, 4]
    let doubled = map4(nums, double)
    let evens = filter4(nums, is_even)
    let squares = map4(nums, square)

    println("doubled: ")
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 4 { print(doubled[i]); print(" "); i = i + 1 }
    println("")
}</lang>

Note: Function references are first-class (<code>let f = double</code>). The type of a function reference is <code>fn(i64) -> i64</code>.
